curl-fetch-axios-converter.formula:
fetch mapping:
  -X METHOD   -> method: 'METHOD'
  -H "N: V"    -> headers: { 'N': 'V' }
  -d BODY      -> body: JSON.stringify({...}) or body: '...'
  -u U:P       -> 'Authorization': 'Basic ' + btoa('U:P')
  -m SEC       -> signal: AbortSignal.timeout(SEC * 1000)
  -F N=V       -> FormData append calls
howTo: Paste your curl command into the input box — multi-line commands work.
Check the parsed summary: method, URL, and header count.
Switch between the Fetch and Axios tabs to preview each output.
Copy the generated code with the copy button.
Paste it into your project inside an async function and adjust as needed.
keyFacts: curl commands are tokenized respecting single quotes, double quotes, and backslash escapes.
A -d body automatically upgrades the method from GET to POST, matching curl behavior.
JSON bodies are detected and re-emitted as pretty-printed JSON.stringify calls.
-G moves data parameters into the URL query string instead of the body.
--data-urlencode percent-encodes values exactly like curl does.

limitations: Browsers block User-Agent, Referer, and Cookie headers — these become comments, not working code.
curl --insecure has no browser equivalent; TLS is always validated by fetch and axios.
Proxy settings, client certificates, and custom CA bundles cannot be translated.
Extremely unusual quoting or shell-specific syntax may not tokenize correctly.
